note: Demographic clones of the 32 base profiles: 2 genders x 5 HUD race categories, 10 clones per profile. Every narrative field is copied verbatim from the base profile; the demographic line is the only field that differs between clones.
underdisclosure_model: Under underdisclosure the respondent withholds up to 3 of the most commonly concealed indicators they have, in this order: b4_exploitation, d2_substance, d6_trauma, d3_mental, b3_legal, b2_harm, d5_medications, c4_relationships. The mask depends only on the base profile, so all ten clones withhold the same indicators. Reported answers never list tri-morbidity; it is derived at scoring.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 34. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Line cook for eleven years, most recently on the hot line of a mid-size restaurant. Completed a culinary certificate at a community college and still keeps the knife roll.
narrative.path: The restaurant closed with two days' notice. Savings covered a motel for a fortnight, then a colleague's sofa, then the shelter.
narrative.finances: Still working 25 hours a week at a catering kitchen. About $600 in savings, no outstanding debts, and a final paycheck from the closed restaurant still owed.
narrative.ties: One adult sibling two states away who calls most weekends. No children.
narrative.routine: Up at 5:30 for the shelter's exit time, a prep shift at the catering kitchen, then the public library until the evening queue. Cooks for the other residents on days off.
narrative.goals: A studio within a bus ride of the catering job. Has priced deposits and is waiting on the withheld paycheck to cover one.
narrative.services: First stay in any shelter. Found the intake process confusing but has kept every document in a labeled folder.
narrative.demeanor: Organized and businesslike; asks precise questions about timelines and wants to know exactly what happens next.
narrative.vignette: Entered a shelter six weeks ago when the restaurant closed with two days' notice. Still working part-time and treats the situation as a temporary gap. Reports no health, safety, or legal concerns.

clones.base_label: Delivery driver living in a car
clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 41. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: A decade of long-haul trucking, then local delivery work closer to home so the alternating weekends could happen.
narrative.path: A $400 rent increase on a one-bedroom. Gave notice rather than fall behind, expecting to find something cheaper within the month; nothing has come up in eight weeks.
narrative.finances: Steady take-home of about $2,100 a month, outpaced by the rent increase. No outstanding debts. Keeps a prepaid phone and a gym membership specifically for showers.
narrative.ties: Two children, ages 9 and 12, living with their other parent in the same city. Alternating weekends together; the children have not been told about the car.
narrative.routine: Parks in a 24-hour lot, gym at 5am for a shower, drives until six, then a fast-food restaurant with free wifi until the lot goes quiet.
narrative.goals: Somewhere with a second bedroom, so the weekends can resume properly instead of being spent at a cinema.
narrative.services: Has not contacted any agency. Looked up eligibility online once and closed the tab.
narrative.demeanor: Proud and self-reliant. Volunteers little, redirects questions toward practical solutions, and is visibly uncomfortable being interviewed at all.
narrative.vignette: Sleeping in a car in a 24-hour lot for the past two months after a rent increase. First episode of homelessness. Still working full hours, showers at the gym before shifts, and reports no health, safety, or legal concerns.

clones.demographic_line: Age 28. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Two years into a nursing program before withdrawing to care for an ill parent, then worked as a home health aide for three years.
narrative.path: Lost the parent and the job within four months of each other. The lease was in the parent's name and was not transferable.
narrative.finances: A small severance and inheritance cover basics for now. No debt, and no income coming in.
narrative.ties: A former roommate who visits the shelter most weeks. No children.
narrative.routine: Sleeps late, walks the same loop to a coffee shop, and sits with a phone until the shelter reopens. Describes every day as identical to the one before.
narrative.goals: Would like to finish the nursing program eventually, but has not looked at the re-entry requirements or set a date.
narrative.services: A grief counsellor was offered at intake. Attended once and did not return.
narrative.demeanor: Flat and tired. Answers fully but without elaboration, and describes the days as 'just getting through.'

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 47. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Seasonal agricultural and construction work since leaving school at 17. Skilled at framing and known on the day-labour circuit.
narrative.path: Housing has always been seasonal — a room during the build months, a tent between contracts. This stretch has run longer because the last contractor folded mid-project.
narrative.finances: Cash day labour two or three days a week, roughly $400 a month. No bank account and no debts being pursued; money kept on a prepaid card.
narrative.ties: A grown child, 26, in another state, in contact once or twice a year. Travels with a dog.
narrative.routine: Up before dawn for the pick-up corner, works if there is work, then back to camp to cook on a propane burner. Repairs other people's gear in the evenings and is sought out for it.
narrative.goals: A room for the winter and a lock-up for the tools. Is not looking for a lease and says so plainly.
narrative.services: Knows the drop-in centre staff by name and uses the showers and mail service. Has declined case management twice.
narrative.demeanor: Talkative and wry, with a long memory for job sites and foremen. Describes homelessness as a rhythm rather than a crisis.
narrative.vignette: Sleeping outdoors in an encampment, homeless on and off for four years across five episodes that track the construction season. Picks up day labour, keeps a tidy camp, and manages hygiene at a drop-in centre. Reports no health or legal concerns.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 52. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Twenty-two years as a warehouse picker at a single company until an automation retrofit cut the shift. High school diploma, no other trade.
narrative.path: Unemployment ran out at fourteen months and the apartment went three months later, after a decade in the same unit.
narrative.finances: No income. Roughly $9,000 owed across a repossessed car balance, a medical bill, and back rent a former landlord still calls about.
narrative.ties: Widowed. Two adult children, one of whom has stopped answering calls.
narrative.routine: Arrives at the shelter early to get the same bunk, watches television in the common room, and goes to bed before the others.
narrative.goals: Wants any warehouse work at all. Applied to sixty postings with no reply and has now stopped applying.
narrative.services: Attended a job club through the shelter for six weeks; stopped after the sessions turned to interview technique.
narrative.demeanor: Formal and a little embarrassed. Apologizes for needing help and recounts the layoff in detail, as though relitigating it.
narrative.vignette: Staying in a shelter for five months. No current income and several creditors in contact. Health is stable and daily needs are manageable, but describes no activities beyond waiting — the warehouse filled the days for two decades and nothing has replaced it.

clones.demographic_line: Age 38. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Rideshare driving and a brief stint managing a phone-repair kiosk. Some community college credits in business, never finished.
narrative.path: The car was rear-ended and the insurance lapsed during the dispute. Without cover the rideshare work stopped, and the rent followed within three months.
narrative.finances: No steady income since the collision. About $2,400 in unpaid tolls, court fines, and a loan from a relative.
narrative.ties: One child, age 6, living with grandparents, with supervised visits twice a month. A close cousin nearby who lends a driveway.
narrative.routine: Moves the car three times a day to avoid tickets, charges the phone at a laundromat, and is always parked and presentable before the visit window.
narrative.goals: Get the car repaired and insured, clear the fines, and move from supervised to unsupervised visits. Can name the order of the steps.
narrative.services: Applied for emergency rental assistance and was denied for missing paperwork. An appeal is pending.
narrative.demeanor: Restless and quick-talking. Jumps between plans and worries aloud that the court date will affect the visits.
narrative.vignette: Sleeping in a car for seven months. An unpaid court fine and accumulated tolls that could make renting harder, money owed to a relative, and no regular income. Reports good health, manageable daily needs, and no safety concerns.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 44. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Fifteen years in hotel housekeeping and laundry. Trained as a certified nursing assistant but let the licence lapse during a previous illness.
narrative.path: Cut to two shifts a week when the hotel changed cleaning contractors. The reduced hours could not cover rent, and a shared apartment ended.
narrative.finances: Two housekeeping shifts a week, about $360 a month, with a disability application pending. No outstanding debts after a hospital charity programme cleared a bill.
narrative.ties: A sibling who helps with paperwork and drives to appointments. No children.
narrative.routine: Two early shifts a week, then long recovery days because of breathlessness. Sits with other residents in the afternoons and helps them fill in forms — the part of the week described as good.
narrative.goals: Get the disability decision, renew the nursing-assistant licence, and stop needing the shelter, in that order.
narrative.services: A shelter nurse checks blood pressure weekly and has been trying to get the prescription refilled for a month.
narrative.demeanor: Warm and chatty about other people, deflecting when asked about own health. Minimizes symptoms with 'it's manageable.'
narrative.vignette: In a shelter for two months. Manages a chronic heart condition and stopped taking a prescribed blood-pressure medication when the last bottle ran out. Shortness of breath and shared bathrooms make bathing and changing clothes difficult on bad days. No substance use, safety, or legal concerns.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 62. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Forty years as a long-distance bus mechanic, the last fifteen as a shift lead. Keeps a framed union card in a bag.
narrative.path: The building was sold and the new owner did not renew a long tenancy. Forty years in the trade did not translate into savings after a divorce settlement.
narrative.finances: About $1,040 a month in pension and Social Security, which does not cover local rents. No debt; saves methodically in cash.
narrative.ties: Three grown children, contact by phone at holidays. A grandchild who mails letters to a general-delivery address.
narrative.routine: Breaks camp at first light so the site is not noticed, reads at the library until noon, then the drop-in centre for a meal and a shower. Keeps to a strict schedule and is irritated when it slips.
narrative.goals: Senior housing. Is on two waiting lists and calls monthly to confirm the place on each.
narrative.services: Registered with the coordinated entry system fourteen months ago and has not been contacted since.
narrative.demeanor: Courteous and precise, with a mechanic's habit of explaining systems. Declines offers of help more than once before accepting.
narrative.vignette: Age 62. Sleeping outdoors under a highway overpass, homeless continuously for just over a year. Receives a pension, manages daily needs independently at a nearby drop-in centre, and reports no health, safety, or legal concerns.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 36. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Call-centre supervisor for six years, promoted twice, until the site closed. Some college, no degree.
narrative.path: Six months of applications after the closure, then eviction. Moved between friends' sofas until the invitations stopped.
narrative.finances: No income. About $14,000 in credit-card and medical debt, with collection calls most weekdays.
narrative.ties: Estranged from parents. A former partner who still texts occasionally. No children.
narrative.routine: Sleeps through the morning, spends the afternoon avoiding the collections calls, and returns to the shelter at the last possible moment before curfew.
narrative.goals: Wants the debt to stop first, and cannot see past it to a job or a flat. Says the order matters and cannot be changed.
narrative.services: Booked a debt-advice appointment twice and missed both.
narrative.demeanor: Guarded and self-deprecating. Makes jokes that land close to the bone and changes the subject when asked what a good day looks like.
narrative.vignette: In a shelter for five months. Four emergency department contacts in six months — two after a bicycle collision, one for a dental abscess, and one ambulance ride after fainting in a queue. A follow-up medication prescribed after the abscess was never filled. No income, multiple creditors in contact, and nothing in the week described as purposeful.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 45. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Auto-body painter for eighteen years, known for custom work. Trained on the job and never held a certificate.
narrative.path: A violent robbery outside a bus depot on the way home from a shift. Six weeks off with the injuries, the shop lost its lease in the same period, and the rent went unpaid.
narrative.finances: Scrap-metal collecting brings in $50 to $150 a week. Roughly $3,000 in old utility and phone bills in collections.
narrative.ties: A sibling in the same city who has offered a couch, in a household that feels unsafe. No children.
narrative.routine: Collects scrap on a fixed route that avoids the depot entirely and weighs in at a yard on Fridays. Sketches custom paint designs in a notebook most evenings, a habit kept from the trade.
narrative.goals: Wants to return to spray work but has not been able to walk into a shop and ask.
narrative.services: Declined a victim-services referral at the hospital. No agency contact since.
narrative.demeanor: Watchful. Sits facing the door, gives short answers at first, and warms only once the questions move away from the robbery.
narrative.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for 18 months. Identifies the robbery — which happened before the housing was lost — as the event that started this period of homelessness, and still avoids that part of the city. Owes money to a former utility provider and has no steady income. Manages daily needs and reports no assaults since becoming homeless.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 64. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Ran a small upholstery business for twenty-five years. Apprenticeship-trained, and still particular about stitching.
narrative.path: Arthritis ended the work. The workshop lease and the flat went together, and Social Security did not cover the rent that followed.
narrative.finances: About $1,190 a month in Social Security and no debt, but rent on a one-bedroom rose past what the cheque covers.
narrative.ties: One adult child overseas, with weekly video calls from a library computer. A long-time friend who stores the tools in a garage.
narrative.routine: Parks behind a supermarket that tolerates it, uses the library computers for the weekly call, and spends afternoons at a senior centre playing cards.
narrative.goals: A ground-floor unit with a bath rather than a shower. Applications are in with two housing authorities.
narrative.services: A senior-services caseworker visits monthly. The relationship is warm but the housing list has not moved in two years.
narrative.demeanor: Dry humour and strong opinions about craftsmanship. Deeply reluctant to be seen as needing care, and describes difficulties as 'slowing down.'
narrative.vignette: Age 64. Sleeping in a vehicle for four months. Advanced arthritis in both hands and a hip injury from a fall make bathing, laundry, and dressing difficult, and the vehicle has no facilities. Receives Social Security and reports no safety or legal concerns.

clones.base_label: Dental assistant who left a partner
clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 33. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Dental assistant; certificate programme completed, then five years at the same practice with a good record.
narrative.path: Left in the night after an escalation, drove four hours, and has not gone back for belongings or the job.
narrative.finances: Left without access to the joint account. About $6,800 owed on a shared credit card the former partner continues to use. No current income.
narrative.ties: No children. A college friend two hours away is the only person who knows the situation.
narrative.routine: Rotates the car between three lots, checks a burner phone for messages from the friend, and runs most mornings — the one routine kept from before.
narrative.goals: A licence in a new state and a practice that does not appear in any shared record. Is afraid of being located.
narrative.services: Has avoided domestic-violence services out of fear the record could be traced, and has not filed a report.
narrative.demeanor: Composed and careful, rehearsing answers before giving them. Watches the door and asks who will be able to see the file.
narrative.vignette: Sleeping in a car for two months after leaving an abusive partner. Manages a chronic stomach condition that worsened over the past year, carries debt on a card still being used by the former partner, and identifies the abuse as the cause of this period of homelessness. Not currently working.

clones.base_label: Gig worker assaulted in a shelter
clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 29. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Warehouse and rideshare work. Left school at 16 and later earned a GED at an adult programme.
narrative.path: A landlord sold the building and the deposit was never returned. Gig income proved too irregular to pass a credit check anywhere else.
narrative.finances: Occasional gig-app shifts, roughly $500 a month. No debts anyone is chasing.
narrative.ties: A younger sibling in foster care, visited monthly without fail. No children.
narrative.routine: Takes early delivery shifts, avoids the shelter's common areas since the assault, and sits outside with headphones until lights out.
narrative.goals: A room with a door that locks. Says this more than once, unprompted.
narrative.services: Reported the assault to shelter staff, who moved the bunk but filed nothing further.
narrative.demeanor: Jumpy and quick to apologize. Scans the room repeatedly and struggles to sit through the full interview.
narrative.vignette: In a shelter for seven months. Six emergency department visits in six months, and an assault in a shelter hallway two months ago. An untreated respiratory condition makes stairs hard, and crowding and shared facilities have made regular bathing and clean clothes difficult. Describes nothing in the week beyond shifts as fulfilling.

narrative.demeanor: Jumpy and quick to apologize. Scans the room repeatedly and struggles to sit through the full interview.

An untreated respiratory condition makes stairs hard, and crowding and shared facilities have made regular bathing and clean clothes difficult. Describes nothing in the week beyond shifts as fulfilling.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 51. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Commercial fishing and then dock work — twenty years on the water, latterly as a deck boss.
narrative.path: The company folded owing two paychecks. A rented room went, then a series of short stays, and eventually the scrub near a boat launch.
narrative.finances: No income. Owes a marina for storage on a boat long since sold, plus a hospital bill.
narrative.ties: Two adult children who do not know where their parent is staying. A former crewmate who shares food.
narrative.routine: Walks the harbour each morning out of habit, sits alone with coffee near a café where the crews used to gather, and returns to the same patch each night.
narrative.goals: Talks about getting back on a boat and has not enquired about a berth in three years.
narrative.services: A street-outreach worker checks in fortnightly. Accepts the food and declines the housing paperwork.
narrative.demeanor: A storyteller — expansive about the past and vague about the present. Deflects health questions with 'the doctors always say that.'
narrative.vignette: Sleeping outdoors near a boat launch, homeless for three years across four episodes. Chronic liver disease diagnosed two years ago, with prescribed medication that frequently goes untaken. No income and several creditors on record, and no activity in the week described as fulfilling.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 40. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Roofing for fifteen years and then bartending when the heights became a problem. Trade-school credits but no certificate.
narrative.path: Cash work dried up over a winter. The rented room went, and drinking that had been weekend-only filled the gap.
narrative.finances: Cash work when hired, roughly $300 a month. No debts being pursued.
narrative.ties: A large extended family in the area, most of whom have stopped taking calls. No children.
narrative.routine: Looks for hire in the morning, drinks in the afternoon if there is money, and plays in a weekly pool league that is the one fixture in the week.
narrative.goals: Says the plan is to get back on a crew in the spring, and has said this for three springs.
narrative.services: Completed a detox programme two years ago and left a residential programme after nine days.
narrative.demeanor: Affable and quick to make the room laugh. Minimizes the drinking as 'social' and grows curt when pressed.
narrative.vignette: In a shelter for nine months. Frequent emergency department and police contact, an assault outside a bar since becoming homeless, and a pending charge that could affect renting. Drinking has previously led to being asked to leave a programme, and hangovers and shared bathrooms make consistent hygiene difficult.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 55. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Thirty years as a machinist at a plant that closed. Certified in CNC operation and retrained twice at the company's expense.
narrative.path: The closure took the pension with it. A heart attack a year later ended the job search, and the medical bills ended the housing.
narrative.finances: No income. A $22,000 hospital bill and a defaulted personal loan.
narrative.ties: Divorced. One adult child in the military, contact about once a year.
narrative.routine: Sleeps in a wooded strip behind a retail park, walks to a fast-food restaurant when the chest pain starts, and otherwise moves as little as possible.
narrative.goals: Wants the heart looked at properly and will not discuss housing until that happens.
narrative.services: Eleven emergency department visits in a year, and has declined every discharge referral offered.
narrative.demeanor: Reserved and precise, and visibly uncomfortable with the interview format. Answers yes or no and offers nothing extra.
narrative.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for two years across five episodes. Repeated emergency department use for an untreated heart condition, no income against substantial medical debt, no activity described as fulfilling, and growing difficulty keeping clean without reliable access to facilities.

clones.base_label: School custodian displaced by a relative
clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 71. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Thirty-four years as a school custodian in the same district. A lifelong resident of one neighbourhood.
narrative.path: A grown child moved in after a separation, took over the household and the finances, and eventually changed the locks.
narrative.finances: The Social Security cheque is redirected to an account the relative controls, leaving effectively no money in hand. A payday loan taken out in their name remains unpaid.
narrative.ties: Four grown children; one forced the move-out and the others have not intervened. A volunteer group provides most current support.
narrative.routine: A volunteer group brings meals to the shelter twice a week; otherwise sits in the common room. Says there is nothing in the week to look forward to.
narrative.goals: Wants the Social Security redirected back, and does not want the relative contacted about it.
narrative.services: An adult-protective-services referral was opened and closed after a refusal to make a statement.
narrative.demeanor: Gentle and apologetic. Reluctant to describe the relative's conduct as abuse and repeatedly says 'they had their reasons.'
narrative.vignette: Age 71. In a shelter for six months after a relative took over the household and forced a move-out. No money in hand, arthritis that limits independent living, difficulty bathing and dressing without assistance, and no activity in the week that feels meaningful. Names the treatment by the relative as a cause of the current homelessness.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 37. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Hair stylist with a steady chair rental and a regular clientele built over eight years.
narrative.path: The relationship ended and the flat was in the partner's name. The chair rental could not be paid without the housing behind it, and the clients drifted.
narrative.finances: Irregular cash from styling in car parks and shelters, about $200 a month. No debts on record.
narrative.ties: No children. A network of acquaintances who trade rides and phone charging.
narrative.routine: Cuts hair for cash during the day, sleeps in the vehicle, and takes an arrangement for a warm bed on the coldest nights. Does other residents' hair free on Sundays, which is described as the good part of the week.
narrative.goals: A chair in a salon again, and a licence renewal that requires a fixed address.
narrative.services: Uses a mobile health van for check-ups and has never been referred to housing.
narrative.demeanor: Charismatic and performative, steering toward humour. Becomes flat and factual when describing the exchanges for shelter.
narrative.vignette: Sleeping in a vehicle for 11 months after a relationship broke down and the shared apartment was lost. Frequent emergency service and police contact, an assault since becoming homeless, and trades sex for a place to stay on cold nights. A chronic lung condition, and drinking that threatens housing stability.

clones.demographic_line: Age 43. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Restaurant dishwashing and then landscaping for a decade. Left school in the tenth grade.
narrative.path: A back injury ended the landscaping work, the kidney diagnosis followed, the children went into kinship care, and the flat went with the income.
narrative.finances: No income. Owes a hospital and a former landlord, with a phone bill in collections.
narrative.ties: Three children in kinship care with a relative; visits stopped two years ago. A camp partner who watches belongings.
narrative.routine: Wakes early with pain, queues for a meal, and spends the day at the camp watching belongings while the camp partner collects cans.
narrative.goals: Wants dialysis to be manageable and the visits restarted, in that order.
narrative.services: Was enrolled in a transitional programme and removed after a positive test. Has not reapplied.
narrative.demeanor: Blunt and impatient with paperwork. Quick to anger at questions that sound like judgment, and protective of the camp partner.
narrative.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for four years across six episodes. Chronic kidney disease with repeated emergency department visits, an assault during an encampment sweep, no income and several creditors, and stimulant use that led to removal from a transitional programme. Describes no activity in the week as fulfilling.

clones.base_label: Former retail manager, no health issues
clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 31. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Two years of college on a scholarship lost after a semester away, then five years in retail management.
narrative.path: A dispute at home ended with a locked door at nineteen, and again at thirty. The second time there was no scholarship to fall back on.
narrative.finances: No income. A defaulted student loan and money owed to people at the shelter.
narrative.ties: Relatives forced the move-out after a dispute. A younger sibling still texts.
narrative.routine: Uses the shelter's computers to job-search in the morning, avoids the person applying pressure in the afternoon, and sleeps badly.
narrative.goals: A retail management role, and enough distance from the shelter to stop being asked for favours.
narrative.services: Has filed two incident reports with shelter staff about the coercion, with no result.
narrative.demeanor: Sharp and analytical, describing their own situation almost clinically. Frustrated at being read as unwell when the problems are practical.
narrative.vignette: In a shelter for eight months after relatives forced a move-out. Frequent emergency and police contact, an assault, a pending charge, and pressure to carry packages for someone at the shelter. No income, no fulfilling activity, and no reliable way to meet basic needs — while reporting no health conditions of any kind.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 68. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Merchant seaman in youth, then twenty-eight years as a night security guard at the same industrial site.
narrative.path: A change-of-address form was never processed and the Social Security stopped. The room was lost within two months, and restoring the benefit now requires an address.
narrative.finances: No current income since the suspension. A hospital bill outstanding.
narrative.ties: No children. A younger relative who has not been located since a move.
narrative.routine: Sleeps sitting up because of the swelling, walks to a coffee stand at opening, and spends the day on a bench near the old workplace.
narrative.goals: Wants the benefit restored and says nothing about housing beyond that.
narrative.services: An appointment with a benefits advocate has been rescheduled three times.
narrative.demeanor: Quiet and stoic, giving brief answers. Repeatedly says the paperwork 'sorted itself out before' — resigned rather than hopeful.
narrative.vignette: Age 68. Sleeping outdoors, homeless continuously for two years. Congestive heart failure with medications that went untaken after benefits lapsed, no income since Social Security was suspended, swelling and fatigue that make washing and changing clothes hard, and no activity in the week described as meaningful.

clones.base_label: Pipefitter who lost the union card
clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 49. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Fifteen years as a union pipefitter with a good rate and steady referrals.
narrative.path: Missed jobs cost the union card, the card cost the income, and the income cost the flat inside a year.
narrative.finances: No income. Child-support arrears and a vehicle repossession balance.
narrative.ties: Two children, now teenagers, living with their other parent. Contact ended four years ago.
narrative.routine: Drinks from waking, collects cans in the afternoon, and returns to a camp under a bridge that has been swept twice this year.
narrative.goals: Talks about a hearing to get the card reinstated and has never scheduled one.
narrative.services: Detox four times in five years, each following an emergency admission.
narrative.demeanor: Alternates between elaborate plans for getting the card back and long silences. Deeply ashamed of the missed support payments.
narrative.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for five years across seven episodes. Chronic liver disease and daily alcohol use that makes housing hard to keep, frequent emergency department visits and repeated assaults at camps, no income against mounting arrears, no fulfilling activity, and no consistent way to bathe or wash clothes.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 61. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Four decades of session and bar work; toured regionally in youth and still reads music.
narrative.path: A long decline in bar work, then a hospital admission for the liver, and a landlord who would not renew after the arrears.
narrative.finances: About $980 a month in Social Security paid on time, plus occasional gig money. No debts.
narrative.ties: A wide circle of musicians who check in. One adult child who visits the shelter monthly.
narrative.routine: Plays a weekly set at the drop-in centre, keeps to the shelter's schedule, does laundry every Thursday, and drinks in the evenings.
narrative.goals: A single room where an instrument can be kept. Expects it to happen and is not anxious about it.
narrative.services: Sees a psychiatrist at a community clinic and attends most appointments.
narrative.demeanor: Gregarious and rehearsed, offering the same three stories readily. Understates both the drinking and the mental-health history.
narrative.vignette: Age 61. In a shelter for ten months. Frequent emergency and police contact, assaults, a pending charge, and pressure to carry items for someone at the shelter. Cirrhosis, long-term alcohol use, and a bipolar diagnosis together. Still receives benefits on time, plays weekly at the drop-in centre, and keeps up with hygiene and laundry.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 46. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Drywall finishing for two decades, working steadily until a back injury and an opioid prescription.
narrative.path: The injury, the prescription, a switch to street supply, and an eviction inside eighteen months.
narrative.finances: No income; sells prescribed medication for cash. Owes a former landlord and a hospital.
narrative.ties: One adult child who has asked for no contact. A dog that stays at the camp.
narrative.routine: Sells what is prescribed at the start of the month, buys what is needed, and spends the rest of the time at the camp with the dog.
narrative.goals: Says the plan is a programme after the winter, and gives a different date each time asked.
narrative.services: Has entered three programmes and completed none. Currently barred from one shelter.
narrative.demeanor: Polite and evasive, agreeing readily with whatever is suggested and giving inconsistent dates.
narrative.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for three years across five episodes. COPD with repeated emergency and crisis service use, assaults at camp, no income, no fulfilling activity, no reliable hygiene, stimulant use affecting housing, and prescribed medication sold rather than taken.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 39. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Grew up in foster care across eleven placements and aged out at 18. Sporadic warehouse and car-wash work since.
narrative.path: Aged out with no placement and has never held a lease. Every stretch of housing since has been someone else's.
narrative.finances: No income. Outstanding fines from citations for sleeping in public, and money owed to people who front supplies.
narrative.ties: No known family. A partner at the camp, and a long-running conflict with another group.
narrative.routine: Moves camp constantly because of the conflict, runs packages to clear a debt, and sleeps in short stretches.
narrative.goals: Wants the debt cleared and the other group to leave them alone. Does not mention housing at all.
narrative.services: Was in the child-welfare system for eleven years and refuses anything that resembles it.
narrative.demeanor: Hypervigilant and fast-talking, testing the interviewer with questions before answering. Unwilling to name who the debts are owed to.
narrative.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for six years across eight episodes. Constant emergency and police contact, repeated assaults, pending charges from public-sleeping citations, and pressure to move packages to clear a debt. No income, no fulfilling activity, no way to keep clean, chronic heart disease, and stimulant use that has caused evictions.

clones.base_label: Former EMT after a mass-casualty call
clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 50. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Emergency medical technician for twelve years, a field training officer, until a mass-casualty call. Never returned to work.
narrative.path: Left the service after the call and could not return, drank through the savings, and the marriage and the house went in the same year.
narrative.finances: No income. A disability claim denied twice on appeal, and medical debt in collections.
narrative.ties: Divorced after the diagnosis. Two adult children who send money occasionally and do not visit.
narrative.routine: Drinks from morning, avoids sirens, and camps far from any road with traffic.
narrative.goals: Says there is no plan and does not expect one.
narrative.services: Two denied disability appeals. Has a lawyer's card and has not called it.
narrative.demeanor: Articulate about clinical details and detached about their own case, describing symptoms almost in the third person.
narrative.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for four years across five episodes. Cirrhosis, alcohol dependence, and PTSD together, with prescribed medication routinely untaken, and the trauma of a call at work named as the cause of this period of homelessness. Also reports frequent emergency use, an assault, no income, and no fulfilling activity.

clones.base_label: Welder who left a violent relationship
clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 42. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Certified welder with offshore experience and a rate that supported a household.
narrative.path: An offshore injury ended the welding, the relationship turned violent during the recovery, and leaving meant leaving everything behind.
narrative.finances: No income. An unpaid protective-order filing fee, restitution owed, and a defaulted car loan.
narrative.ties: No contact with family. One friend who holds mail.
narrative.routine: Sleeps in daylight where it feels safer, uses at night, and moves before dawn.
narrative.goals: Cannot answer the question; changes the subject to the protective order each time it is asked.
narrative.services: A protective order was granted and expired. No follow-up services were taken up.
narrative.demeanor: Flat affect and long pauses. Describes the relationship only when asked directly, and then in detail.
narrative.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for seven years across nine episodes that began with an abusive relationship. Frequent emergency and police contact, an assault since becoming homeless, a pending charge, no income, no fulfilling activity, no reliable hygiene, and co-occurring chronic pain, methamphetamine use, and a schizoaffective diagnosis.

narrative.background: Left school at 15. A decade of short-term kitchen jobs, never longer than eight months at one place.

narrative.ties: Relatives forced the move-out at 19. Two siblings whose whereabouts are unknown.

narrative.services: Known to every outreach team in the district and has never held a housing placement.

narrative.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for eight years across ten episodes after relatives forced a move-out. Constant emergency and police contact, assaults, a pending charge, coercion, no income, no fulfilling activity, and no way to meet basic needs — alongside chronic asthma, heroin use, and a depressive disorder together. clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 44. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Trained as a paralegal and worked eight years in litigation support, with a reputation for thoroughness.
narrative.path: The firm collapsed with the supervising attorney's disbarment. No reference could be obtained, the applications stopped, and nine years followed.
narrative.finances: No income; sells prescribed medication to cover camp debts. Judgments from two creditors.
narrative.ties: One adult child in another state who has blocked contact. No local ties.
narrative.routine: Sells the month's prescription in the first week, drinks the rest of the time, and moves between three underpasses.
narrative.goals: Describes the housing system's failures in detail and declines to name anything wanted.
narrative.services: Has been assessed eleven times by six agencies and can quote the score from each.
narrative.demeanor: Precise with dates and documents, and openly cynical about services after years of navigating them.
narrative.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for nine years across twelve episodes. Constant emergency and police contact, assaults, pending charges, coercion, no income, no fulfilling activity, and no reliable hygiene, with emphysema, alcohol and stimulant use, and a bipolar diagnosis together, and prescribed medication sold rather than taken. Does not name a single triggering trauma.

clones.demographic_line: Age 47. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Merchant marine from nineteen until a shipboard injury at thirty. No shore trade to fall back on.
narrative.path: The injury ended the career and there was no transferable qualification. The eleven years since have been continuous, with no indoor stay longer than a night.
narrative.finances: No income. Debts to hospitals, camp lenders, and a former landlord, plus unpaid citations.
narrative.ties: No known living family. A dog that has been a constant for six years.
narrative.routine: Wakes with the dog, walks a fixed route for bottles and food, and returns to the same underpass. Has not slept indoors in four years.
narrative.goals: Wants somewhere the dog is allowed, and has been told repeatedly that this is not possible.
narrative.services: Offered congregate shelter many times and refuses it because of the dog.
narrative.demeanor: Exhausted and matter-of-fact. Answers every question without hesitation and expects nothing to come of it.
narrative.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, chronically homeless for eleven years. Every one of the sixteen vulnerability indicators is flagged — the highest score reachable by a respondent under 60, since the one remaining point is the pre-survey age indicator.

clones.race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous
clones.demographic_line: Age 73. Gender: Male. Race: American Indian, Alaska Native, or Indigenous.

narrative.background: Ran a neighbourhood grocery for thirty years and never worked for anyone else. Knew every customer by name.
narrative.path: The building was sold to a developer; the business and the flat above it went together, and the supplier debts followed the closure.
narrative.finances: Social Security garnished for an old business debt, leaving almost nothing. Further debts to former suppliers.
narrative.ties: Widowed. One adult child who died, and a grandchild who has not been located.
narrative.routine: Sets out goods from a trolley on the same corner each morning as though the shop were still open, and is moved along by the afternoon.
narrative.goals: Talks about reopening and gives a date that has already passed.
narrative.services: Refuses the shelter as charity. Accepts a weekly meal from a volunteer van.
narrative.demeanor: Formal and proud, insisting on being addressed by a trade title, and refusing to describe any part of the past as abuse.
narrative.vignette: Age 73. Sleeping outdoors, homeless for six years across seven episodes. Scores the pre-survey age indicator and every History, Risks and Socialization indicator, with co-occurring heart failure, alcohol use and cognitive decline, and medications that go unmanaged — but does not identify abuse or trauma as the cause of homelessness.

narrative.background: Career carpenter and union steward, respected enough to be sent to arbitrate other sites' disputes.
narrative.path: A workplace assault, a long recovery, a foreclosure during it, and fourteen years since without a lease.
narrative.finances: No income after benefits lapsed. Debts to hospitals, lenders, and a former landlord.
narrative.ties: Estranged from three adult children after the decline. No current contact with anyone outside the camp.
narrative.routine: Cannot give a consistent account of a day. Is found within the same three blocks and does not always recognise the outreach worker.
narrative.goals: Answers with a job that ended in the 1990s.
narrative.services: Assessed many times over fourteen years; the records do not agree with one another.
narrative.demeanor: Disoriented about sequence and dates but vivid about the distant past. Agrees with most questions, which makes verification difficult.
narrative.vignette: Age 66. Sleeping outdoors, chronically homeless for fourteen years. The maximum score the tool can produce: the pre-survey age indicator plus all sixteen vulnerability indicators.

narrative.background: Career carpenter and union steward, respected enough to be sent to arbitrate other sites' disputes.
narrative.path: A workplace assault, a long recovery, a foreclosure during it, and fourteen years since without a lease.
narrative.finances: No income after benefits lapsed. Debts to hospitals, lenders, and a former landlord.
narrative.ties: Estranged from three adult children after the decline. No current contact with anyone outside the camp.
narrative.routine: Cannot give a consistent account of a day. Is found within the same three blocks and does not always recognise the outreach worker.
narrative.goals: Answers with a job that ended in the 1990s.
narrative.services: Assessed many times over fourteen years; the records do not agree with one another.
narrative.demeanor: Disoriented about sequence and dates but vivid about the distant past. Agrees with most questions, which makes verification difficult.
